cases.name: b1.minkowski_is_vacuum
cases.notes: fixes the overall normalisation of the Plebanski map in these units
cases.reference: eta_{mu nu} maps to eps = mu = I and zero magnetoelectric coupling

cases.name: b1.isotropic_forward
cases.reference: g = diag(-1,a,a,a) gives eps = mu = sqrt(a) I

cases.name: b1.gordon_optical_metric_speed
cases.notes: this is a RAY statement for a medium that need not be impedance matched, and is a different claim from the Plebanski map
cases.reference: the static isotropic Gordon metric diag(-1/n^2,1,1,1) has null coordinate speed 1/n

cases.computed_description: eps != mu: the medium is not impedance matched, so it is birefringent in the general case and no single pseudo-Riemannian metric reproduces full Maxwell propagation in it. An optical (Gordon) metric may still describe rays.
cases.name: b1.plain_dielectric_not_metric_representable
cases.notes: separates full-Maxwell metric equivalence from ray-level optical metrics
cases.reference: a non-magnetic dielectric (eps = 4I, mu = I) is rejected as metric-representable, despite having a well-defined Gordon optical metric

cases.name: b1.anisotropic_forward
cases.reference: g = diag(-1,2,3,5) gives eps^ii = sqrt(30)/g_ii

cases.name: b1.conformal_invariance
cases.notes: sqrt(-g) contributes Omega^4, g^{ij} contributes Omega^-2 and 1/g_00 contributes Omega^-2, so the three cancel exactly. This is WHY the inverse can only return a conformal class
cases.reference: the medium is unchanged under g -> Omega^2 g, for Omega^2 = 0.25, 0.5, 2, 7

cases.name: b1.roundtrip_conformal
cases.notes: componentwise equality is deliberately NOT demanded: the forward map discards the conformal factor, so requiring it would be demanding information the physics does not determine
cases.reference: g -> (eps,mu) -> ghat recovers the CONFORMAL CLASS of g

cases.name: b1.roundtrip_factor_is_nontrivial
cases.reference: at least one round trip returns a representative with Omega^2 != 1, confirming the conformal test is not a disguised equality test

cases.name: b1.null_cone_equivalence
cases.notes: a conformally invariant observable, so this is the right thing to demand of a reconstruction
cases.reference: the reconstructed metric has the same null coordinate speeds along each axis as the original

cases.computed_description: 3 detected. uniaxial birefringent: not_metric_representable; axion/Tellegen: not_metric_representable; asymmetric eps: not_metric_representable;
cases.name: b1.nonmetric_detected
cases.notes: the requirement is that the code refuse, not that it produce a best-fit metric with no warning
cases.reference: constitutive tensors that no single pseudo-Riemannian metric can produce -- birefringent, axion/Tellegen, and skewon-like -- are each REPORTED rather than fitted

cases.name: b1.valid_medium_accepted
cases.notes: guards against a classifier that rejects everything
cases.reference: an impedance-matched symmetric medium with no magnetoelectric coupling is accepted and reconstructed

cases.name: b1.warp_subluminal_medium_exists
cases.reference: for v_s = 0.2 the Alcubierre metric has an equivalent medium at every sampled point

cases.name: b1.warp_is_bianisotropic
cases.notes: a realizability fact: no arrangement of ordinary dielectrics can reproduce this without magnetoelectric coupling
cases.reference: the warp medium has a nonzero magnetoelectric vector w, i.e. it is bianisotropic, not a simple dielectric

cases.name: b1.warp_inverse_reports_unsupported
cases.reference: reconstructing a metric from a magnetoelectric medium is reported as unsupported in B1 rather than approximated

cases.computed_description: 121 of 321 sample points have no equivalent medium; first at x = -3
cases.name: b1.superluminal_medium_fails_reported
cases.notes: this is the central realizability limitation of the whole programme: the superluminal regime is exactly the regime in which the metric-to-medium correspondence breaks down in this frame. It is the same v_s f > 1 condition that costs Program A its coordinate observers
cases.reference: for v_s = 2 there are points where g_00 >= 0 and NO equivalent medium exists, and the map reports this instead of returning a value

cases.name: b1.generic.test_scalar
cases.reference: the constitutive mapping instantiates with a custom scalar having no ordering, no equality and no implicit double conversion

cases.name: b1.sensitivity.metric_parameters
cases.notes: the constitutive mapping is templated, so OTI channels flow from the metric parameters through to the medium with no extra code
cases.parameters: v=0.2, R=3, sigma=2 at the wall x=3
cases.reference: d eps_yy / d(v, R, sigma) through the Plebanski map matches centred finite differences

cases.name: b1.sensitivity.refractive_index
cases.notes: an analytic reference, not a finite-difference one
cases.reference: for eps = mu = n^2 I the reconstruction gives h = n^4 I and dh/dn = 4n^3, both matched by HyPAD

cases.name: b1.sensitivity.conformal_normalisation
cases.notes: sharper than comparing values at discrete Omega: it asserts the derivative vanishes identically, which a near-invariance would fail
cases.reference: d eps / d Omega == 0: the differential form of conformal invariance of the forward map

cases.name: b1.sensitivity.observable_null_speed
cases.notes: an observable derived from the effective metric, not a raw component
cases.reference: the null coordinate speed 1/n^2 of the reconstructed medium, and its derivative -2/n^3, both match HyPAD

title: Metric to electromagnetic constitutive response: Plebanski-Tamm forward map, conformal-class inverse, and non-metric detection
